error.network: Homewarden cannot be reached. Check that the container is running.
error.internal: Homewarden hit an internal error. The container log has the details.
error.unauthorized: Your session has ended. Sign in again.
error.forbidden: Your role does not allow this.
error.csrf: The request was blocked as a possible forgery. Reload the page.
error.rate_limited: Too many attempts. Try again in {retryAfter} seconds.
error.mfa_required: Enter the code from your authenticator app.
error.invalid_code: That code is not valid. Check that your device's clock is correct.
error.setup_done: Setup was already completed. Reload the page to sign in.
error.invalid_setup_token: The setup token is wrong. Copy it again from the container log; it changes on every restart.
error.invalid_username: Usernames are 2 to 64 characters: letters, digits and . _ - @
error.password_mismatch: The two passwords do not match.
error.last_admin: This is the last admin. Make another user an admin first.
error.cannot_delete_self: You cannot delete your own account.
error.role_name_taken: A role with this name already exists.
error.role_in_use: Users still have this role. Give them another role first.
setup.title: Create the admin account
setup.intro: This is a new Homewarden. The first account you create here is the admin.
setup.tokenHint: Printed in the container log. On Unraid: Docker tab, click the Homewarden icon, Logs. Elsewhere: docker logs homewarden.
setup.usernameHint: You can pick any name, it does not have to be admin.
login.codeHint: The 6-digit code from your authenticator app.
nav.label: Main navigation
devices.title: Devices
settings.title: Settings
account.passwordOthers: Other devices signed in to this account are signed out.
account.totpIntro: Optional. When on, signing in also needs a code from an authenticator app such as Aegis, Google Authenticator or 1Password.
account.totpScan: Scan this code with your authenticator app, then enter the code it shows.
account.totpQr: QR code for the authenticator app
account.totpManual: Or enter this key by hand:
account.totpDisablePw: Enter your password to turn it off
users.intro: Everyone who can sign in. What they can do depends on their role.
users.newPasswordHint: Leave empty to keep the current password. Setting one signs the user out everywhere.
roles.intro: A role is a set of permissions. Admin, Operator and Viewer are built in; add your own for anything in between.
roles.name: Name
permDesc.devices.view: see devices, versions and available updates
permDesc.devices.manage: add, configure, ignore and remove devices
permDesc.credentials.manage: add and change passwords, keys and tokens
devices.emptyText: Add a device by its address, or scan your network and pick what to monitor from the inbox.
devices.search: Search by name, address or group
stateHint.reachable: Answers on the network, but its service is not up yet or is still settling
stateHint.ready: Fully up: the service answers and stayed up for the settle time
deviceForm.name: Name
deviceForm.presenceIntro: A device counts as online only after the second check passes and stays up for the settle time. A ping alone does not mean it has finished booting.
deviceForm.readyHint: For example TCP 22 for SSH on a Pi, or the web interface of OctoPrint.
deviceForm.settleHint: How long the service must stay up before scans start.
inbox.intro: Devices found on your network. Nothing here is monitored until you add it.
inbox.emptyText: Scan your network to find devices. Integrations added later will put what they find here too.
ignored.intro: Devices you chose to ignore. Restore one to move it back to the inbox.
ignored.emptyText: Devices you ignore in the inbox are kept here so they can be restored later.
discovery.title: Scan the network
discovery.intro: Homewarden pings every address in the range and tries a few common ports for devices that block ping. Found devices go to the inbox.
discovery.rangeHint: CIDR notation, at most 1024 addresses, e.g. 192.168.90.0/24.
discovery.result: {alive} of {scanned} addresses answered, {new} new in the inbox.
detail.noChecks: No checks; the state comes from the device it runs on.
detail.manageHint: Ignoring keeps the device in the Ignored list so it can be restored. Deleting also removes its history.
detail.inInbox: This device is in the inbox and not monitored yet.
detail.isIgnored: This device is ignored and not monitored.
error.invalid_host: The address must not contain spaces or slashes.
error.host_required: Enter an address, or turn off the network check.
error.invalid_probe: Check the online detection settings: a TCP check needs a port, an HTTP check a URL starting with http:// or https://.
error.invalid_parent: A device cannot run on itself.
error.no_presence_check: This device has no network check.
error.invalid_cidr: Enter a valid IPv4 range of at most 1024 addresses, e.g. 192.168.1.0/24.
cred.intro: Passwords, API tokens and SSH keys, stored encrypted. They are never shown again after saving; devices refer to them by name.
cred.name: Name
cred.emptyText: Add an SSH key to connect to Linux devices, or a token for devices with an API such as OctoPrint.
cred.usernameHint: The login name on the device. A device can override it.
cred.generate: Generate a new key in Homewarden (recommended)
cred.publicKey: Public key (goes into authorized_keys on the device)
cred.keepSecret: Leave empty to keep the stored value.
cred.keyCreatedText: Homewarden keeps the private key. Put this public key on a device with Install key on the device page, or add it to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys yourself.
credTypeHint.ssh_key: For logging in to Linux devices over SSH.
credTypeHint.password: For SSH with a password, or services with a login.
credTypeHint.token: For APIs such as OctoPrint, Proxmox or UniFi.
conn.title: Connection
conn.intro: How Homewarden logs in to this device to read versions and run updates.
conn.sudoHint: Updates need root. With this on, Homewarden runs them through sudo without a password prompt, so the user needs a matching sudoers rule. A rule that only allows the package manager is enough.
conn.keyChangedTitle: The device's SSH host key changed
conn.keyChangedText: Pinned: {expected}. Now: {got}. This is expected after reinstalling the device. If you did not, something may be intercepting the connection.
conn.sudoNo: needs a password (not usable for updates)
conn.firstKey: First connection: the host key was pinned. A different key later will block the connection.
install.title: Install SSH key
install.intro: Homewarden logs in to {host} once with a password, adds its key, and checks that key login works.
install.step1: The password is used for this one login and is not stored.
install.step2: The public key is added to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of the user.
install.step3: The device is then set to use the key.
error.invalid_private_key: This is not a readable private key. Password-protected keys are not supported.
error.credential_name_taken: A credential with this name already exists.
error.credential_in_use: {n} devices still use this credential. Change them first.
error.connection_not_configured: Set a credential for this device first.
error.host_key_changed: The SSH host key of the device changed.
error.ssh_auth_failed: Login refused. Check the user and the credential, and that the key is in authorized_keys.
error.ssh_unreachable: The SSH port does not answer. Check the address, the port and that SSH is enabled.
updates.title: Updates
updates.emptyText: Devices are scanned when they come online and every few hours. Devices without an integration are not scanned.
warnHint.reboots: The device restarts at the end and is offline for a moment. Homewarden waits for it.
warnHint.restarts-services: Services on the device (e.g. its web interface) restart during the update, so it may not answer for a few seconds. Nothing to do for you.
warnHint.restarts-host: The host restarts, and everything running on it with it.
warnHint.restarts-container: The container is stopped, removed and started again from the new image.
warnHint.self: This is where Homewarden runs. Update it from the host instead.
sw.title: Software
sw.notifyOnlyHint: Homewarden shows this update but does not run it, for example because the device it runs on would go down.
sw.eol: This system stopped receiving updates on {date}. Plan an upgrade to a supported release.
sw.rebootRequired: A reboot is required to finish earlier updates.
sw.neverScanned: Not scanned yet. Scans start when the device comes online; or press Scan now.
sw.force: Update even if the device is busy
integ.presenceHint: Sets the checks this integration recommends, such as waiting for SSH.
jobs.emptyText: Scans, updates and backups show up here with their full output.
market.title: Integrations
market.intro: Integrations teach Homewarden about a kind of device. Install only what you use; each one runs sandboxed with the permissions shown before installing.
market.sourcesIntro: One URL per line, pointing at a folder with index.json. GitHub raw URLs and your own Gitea work. Built-in integrations are always available.
perm2.ssh: run commands on the device over SSH
perm2.docker: use the Docker API of the device
perm2.httpDevice: call web APIs on the device
error.invalid_source: Sources must start with https:// or http:// and be in the list of catalog sources.
error.catalog_unreachable: The catalog could not be read.
error.integration_in_use: Devices still use this integration. Switch them to another type first.
error.no_integration: Pick an integration for this device first.
factWarn.undervoltage: The Pi reported undervoltage. A weak power supply causes failed prints and corrupted SD cards.
backups.title: Backups
backups.stale: {n} devices without a backup in the last {d} days
backups.noDevicesTitle: No devices that can be backed up
backups.noDevicesText: Devices whose integration supports backups (for example OctoPrint) show up here.
backups.noTargets: No targets yet. Add an SMB share or a folder mounted into the container.
backups.typeSmb: SMB share (Windows share, Unraid share, NAS)
backups.folderHint: Optional. Each device gets its own subfolder below it.
backups.loginHint: A credential of type Password with the share user name.
backups.pathHint: For example /backups when the Unraid template maps the Backups folder.
backups.testOk: Homewarden wrote, read and deleted a test file.
backups.needTarget: Add a backup target first under
backups.beforeUpdate: Back up to this target before every update
guards.title: Busy rules
guards.intro: Extra checks before updates on this device. A rule that fires blocks the update, or only writes a warning to the log. Forcing an update skips them.
guards.name: Name
guards.commandHint: Busy when the command exits with 0. Runs over the device's SSH connection.
error.target_incomplete: Fill in server and share, or an absolute folder path.
error.target_name_taken: A target with this name already exists.
error.target_failed: The target could not be used.
error.no_backup_support: This device's integration cannot create backups.
error.guard_incomplete: Every rule needs a command, or a URL starting with http:// or https://.
auto.title: Automation
auto.hint.manual: Homewarden shows updates; you start them.
auto.hint.auto: Every scan that finds updates starts them right away. Scans run when the device comes online and every 6 hours.
auto.hint.scheduled: At the scheduled time Homewarden scans and then updates. If the device is offline, it runs as soon as the device is back.
auto.cronHint: Minute hour day month weekday, in the container's time zone (TZ). Empty = off.
auto.scopeHint: Busy rules, the integration's own guard and backup before update apply as usual. Notify-only components are never touched.
auto.pending: Waiting for the device to come online: {list} (since {since}).
auto.apiHint: Create an API token under Settings, API tokens, then:
auto.mqttHint: Or with MQTT enabled, publish scan, backup, update or update security to {topic}.
tokens.intro: Personal tokens for scripts and Home Assistant. A token can do what your role allows. Send it as Authorization: Bearer <token>.
tokens.copyNow: Copy this token now. It is not shown again.
mqtt.intro: Publishes each device's state and number of updates, and takes commands. Home Assistant can use these topics in MQTT sensors and buttons.
error.invalid_cron: This is not a valid schedule. Use five fields, for example 0 3 * * 0 for Sundays at 03:00.
error.invalid_broker: The broker must start with tcp://, ssl:// or ws://.
factWarn.datastore_full: A datastore is almost full. Prune or add space before backups start failing.
factWarn.backup_old: The newest backup in a datastore is older than the limit set for this device.
factWarn.backup_errors: Backup, verify or sync tasks failed in the last 7 days. The job log lists them.
factWarn.disk_problems: A disk reports errors, is disabled or runs hot. Check the Main page in Unraid.
conn.needHost: Set an address for this device to use SSH, or use the agent.
agent.name: Agent
agent.intro: A small program on the device that connects out to Homewarden. Use it when Homewarden cannot reach the device directly (other network, firewall) or you prefer it to SSH. Everything that works over SSH works over the agent; it runs as root (Windows: SYSTEM).
agent.usePresence: Use the agent for online detection
agent.commandIntro: Run this once on the device. It downloads the agent from Homewarden, connects it to this device and installs it as a service.
agent.insecure: Homewarden uses a self-signed HTTPS certificate
agent.tokenHint: The command contains a one-time token, valid for 24 hours. Creating a new one replaces it.
factWarn.unifi_offline: One or more UniFi devices are offline or not adopted.
install.sudo: Also allow updates: add this sudoers rule
install.sudoHint: Uses the same password once through sudo. The rule is checked with visudo before it is saved.
restore.title: Restore backup
restore.intro: Puts {name} from {when} back onto a device.
restore.ontoHint: Pick another device of the same type to set up a replacement, e.g. a freshly flashed OctoPi.
restore.warning: The device's current settings are replaced by the backup and it restarts. Running jobs on the device should be finished first.
restore.started: Restore started. The job log shows the progress.
error.no_restore_support: This device's integration cannot restore backups.
notify.intro: Where Homewarden tells you about new updates, failed jobs, warnings and devices that stay offline. Each channel picks its own events.
notify.baseUrlHint: Messages link to the device or job. Use the address you open Homewarden with, e.g. https://homewarden.lan.
notifyEvHint.jobs: with the end of the log
notifyEvHint.warnings: disks, undervoltage, old backups, end of life
notifyEvHint.offline: only for devices with an offline limit (Automation card)
auto.offline: Notify when offline for more than (minutes)
auto.offlineHint: 0 = never. Leave 0 for devices that are often off on purpose, like a printer Pi.
mqtt.haHint: Every device appears in Home Assistant with an online sensor, an update count and buttons for scan and updates.
error.channel_incomplete: Fill in the fields this channel type needs.
mon.title: Monitors
mon.emptyText: Watch web pages, ports, DNS records and scripts that report in, with response times and alerts.
mon.invert: Fail if the text is found instead
mon.pushIntro: A script or device calls the push URL regularly. If no call arrives within 1.5 intervals, the monitor goes down. The URL appears after saving.
mon.pushHint: Call this URL from your script (curl, wget, Home Assistant). status=down reports a failure.
mon.public: Show on the public status page
maint.title: Maintenance windows
maint.intro: While a window is active, no alerts are sent for the device (or for everything) and the status page shows the maintenance.
status.title: Public status page
status.intro: A page without login at /status that shows the monitors marked public: their state and the last 24 hours. Addresses and error messages are not shown.
status.off: This status page is not enabled.
error.monitor_incomplete: Fill in the target for this monitor type (http:// or https:// URL, host, port).
error.invalid_window: Enter a title and an end after the start.
res.title: Resources
factWarn.disk_full: A file system is more than 90% full.
factWarn.hot: A temperature sensor reports 80 °C or more.
factWarn.smart_failing: A disk failed its SMART self-assessment. Replace it soon.
sw.noChangelog: No change notes available for this component.
sw.chooseIntro: Currently {current}. Pick the version to switch to; older ones roll back.
sw.chooseHint: The container is recreated with the same settings on the chosen tag. Versions marked on this host need no download.
error.not_supported: This integration does not support that.
sso.title: Single sign-on (OIDC)
sso.intro: Sign in with Authentik, Authelia, Keycloak or any OpenID Connect provider. Local accounts keep working, so you cannot lock yourself out.
sso.redirect: Redirect URI to register at the provider:
sso.issuerHint: Authentik: the provider OpenID Configuration Issuer. Authelia: your Authelia address.
sso.label: Button label
roles.groupsHint: Leave all unticked to allow every device. Ticked: users with this role only see and act on devices in these groups.
roles.noGroups: No device groups yet. Set a group on devices first.
error.oidc_incomplete: Enter the issuer URL and client ID.
error.oidc_discovery: The provider could not be reached or is not an OpenID Connect issuer.
net.intro: What your firewall and VLAN rules have to allow. Rules go from the Homewarden container address to the devices, not the other way round, except the web port.
net.vlan: Devices in another VLAN: allow the Homewarden container IP to reach that VLAN on the ports below. On Unraid with bridge networking that is the Unraid server IP; with br0 or a custom network it is the container’s own IP.
discovery.rangesHint: One range per row in CIDR notation, e.g. 192.168.90.0/24 for one VLAN and 192.168.20.0/24 for another. At most 1024 addresses per range and 4096 per scan. Several ranges can also be pasted comma-separated.
conn.inheritedHint: This device uses the connection from the integration setup (credential, user, port and sudo). Pick a credential here only if this device needs its own.
integ.sharedHint: Credentials and shared options for all {name} devices are set once in the integration setup. Here you only set what belongs to this device.
integSetup.title: Set up {name}
integSetup.intro: These values apply to every device that uses this integration. A device only needs its own value where it differs.
integSetup.connectionHint: Devices without a credential of their own connect with this. Devices using the agent are not affected.
integSetup.settingsHint: Empty fields use the integration's built-in default.
integSetup.nothing: This integration has nothing to set up.
integSetup.noDevices: No device uses this integration yet. Pick it in a device's Integration card.
integSetup.saved: Saved. All devices of this integration use the new values from the next run.
integSetup.guide: Setup guide: where to get keys and tokens
integSetup.perDevice: Set per device in its Integration card: {list}.
integ.overrides: Override shared settings for this device
integ.overridesHint: Leave a field on Default to use the integration setup.
cred.tokenId: Token ID (only for Proxmox and PBS)
cred.tokenIdHint: Leave empty for API keys that are a single value, like OctoPrint or UniFi.
netinfo.title: Network
market.allInstalled: Everything from the catalog is installed.
activity.title: Activity
activity.intro: Everything Homewarden ran or is running: scans, updates, backups and restores, with the full output of each run.
activity.waiting: waiting for the device's previous job
mon.suggestIntro: Devices without a monitor. Web interfaces get an HTTP check with certificate expiry, others their port or ping. Devices that are off right now are not preselected, so a printer that is only sometimes on does not start as down.
upd.title: Update {name}
upd.introAll: Everything that can be updated ({n}) will be installed:
upd.whatHappens: What happens during the update (nothing to do for you):
upd.lastBlocked: The last update was not run
upd.started.blocked: Update not run: the device was busy.
factWarn.ssh_needed: Installing updates needs SSH: the Proxmox API can only list them. Set up SSH as root in the Connection card below, or once for all Proxmox hosts in the integration setup (Integrations, Proxmox VE, Set up).
warnHint.needs-reboot: Takes effect after the next restart. Homewarden does not restart the device; do it when it suits you.
agentSsh.title: Install the agent on {name}
agentSsh.intro: Homewarden logs in over SSH once, installs the agent as root and lets it register. From then on the device talks to Homewarden by itself and needs no open port. Linux only (Raspberry Pi, Debian/Ubuntu, Proxmox, Unraid); for Windows use the install command.
agentSsh.modePassword: User and password (only for this step, not saved)
agentSsh.passwordHint: Use root, or a user with full sudo rights. The password is used for this login and sudo only.
agentSsh.savedHint: Uses the credential from the Connection card or the integration setup. It must log in as root, or have sudo without password.
agentSsh.server: Homewarden address as the device reaches it
agentSsh.serverHint: The agent connects here. Use the LAN address (e.g. http://192.168.90.81:8080), not a name only your browser knows.
agentSsh.ok: Agent installed. It registers within a few seconds; the device then uses the agent instead of SSH.
